subject: Networking surface area: choosing connection pattern for NetBridge private deployment
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Anita Patel <anita.patel@netbridge.com>, networkops@netbridge.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Networking surface area: choosing connection pattern for NetBridge private deployment

Hi Anita / NetBridge ops team,

Thanks again for the time earlier — quick follow-up from our architecture review. NetBridge is targeting a private deployment of Redwood inside a dedicated AWS account (single region to start, multi-account in roadmap). The core ask from your team is: which connectivity pattern should we design for day 1 to meet security, latency, and operational simplicity goals — VPC Peering, AWS PrivateLink (Interface VPC Endpoint), or a site-to-site VPN between your VPC and Redwood's dedicated account?

I've attached a short connectivity matrix (connectivity-matrix.csv) and sketched a couple of topologies. Could you confirm the constraints below so we make a firm recommendation?

- IP overlap risk: do you anticipate overlapping RFC1918 ranges with NetBridge accounts?
- Expected egress throughput from NetBridge to Redwood (baseline and peak)?
- Do you need cross-region failover or multi-AZ only for day 1?
- Procurement constraints: are cross-account VPC peering acceptible, or do you require endpoint-based access?

Prelim decider notes (for transparency):
- PrivateLink gives us strong isolation and does not require peering or route-table changes in your VPC — good for multi-account setups and reduces IP collision surface.
- VPC Peering is simple and low-latency but can be painful if you expect overlapping addresses or complex transitive routing needs.
- Site-to-site VPN is the quickest to stand up for proof-of-concept but has predictable latency variation and is harder to scale for many subnets/addresses.

Can you respond with the bullets above? Once we have that we'll recommend a primary pattern and an operational runbook for day 1.

Thanks,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Partner Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: connectivity-matrix.csv (CSV), design-notes.pdf (stub)

From: Anita Patel <anita.patel@netbridge.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: networkops@netbridge.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Networking surface area: choosing connection pattern for NetBridge private deployment

Sergio — thanks for the note. Quick answers from our side: 

- IP overlap: likely. Our central infra team reserves many RFC1918 ranges and we have a few older tenant ranges that may overlap with vendor accounts. We cannot renumber at this stage.
- Throughput: baseline 200 Mbps, burst up to 1.5 Gbps for short periods (daily batch windows).
- Cross-region: not required day 1; single region deployment is fine.
- Procurement: we prefer not to accept inbound peering requests that change our route tables; prefer endpoint-based patterns where possible.

A couple of extra constraints — we require Mutual TLS on any control-plane connections and need audit logs for every session initiated to our VPC. Also looking for an approach that minimizes egress NAT complexity.

Anita
Anita Patel
Head of Cloud Ops, NetBridge Systems

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Networking surface area: choosing connection pattern for NetBridge private deployment

Thanks for the details Anita — the constraints are helpful. Short recommendation + rationale below; I can expand into a runbook if we decide to go forward with the pattern.

Recommendation (day 1): AWS PrivateLink (Interface VPC Endpoints) hosted in Redwood's dedicated account, with a small set of whitelisted service endpoints for the control plane and inference endpoints.

Rationale:
- IP overlap: PrivateLink avoids route-table changes and does not require peering; it eliminates the IP collision surface which you flagged as a blocker.
- Throughput: Interface endpoints support ENI bandwidth; for your 1.5 Gbps bursts we should plan for a small fleet behind a network load balancer and load-test the ENI count/instance sizes. If throughput needs exceed ~5 Gbps sustained we can discuss an ingress transit approach, but for day 1 the endpoint pattern is in-range.
- Security/Audit: PrivateLink connections originate from your VPC to our endpoint and can be proxied through an NLB with TLS termination on our side. We can additionally require mTLS between your service and our control-plane endpoints; flow logs + our access logs will be dual-recorded (your VPC Flow Logs + our endpoint logs) satisfying the audit requirement.
- Procurement / operational simplicity: No route-table updates on your side, no cross-account peering approvals, fewer networking tickets.

Tradeoffs to note:
- Cost: PrivateLink has per-GB and per-hour endpoint costs and charges for data processed through the interface endpoint on both sides. We'll include a cost estimate in the matrix.
- Latency: Slightly higher than peering (due to ENI/NLB) but predictable and generally within 1–5 ms extra for same-region traffic.
- DNS & discovery: We will publish service DNS names and provide a DNS override guide for your infra team.

Attachments: plnk-topology.png (topology sketch). I'm happy to sketch a fallback plan using S2S VPN for PoC if you prefer faster time-to-proof.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Networking surface area: choosing connection pattern for NetBridge private deployment

Anita / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and Karthik for the notes. Summary + next steps below (action items are focused on day 1 delivery):

Decision: proceed with PrivateLink for day 1 (subject to throughput validation). We will treat a site-to-site VPN as a short-lived PoC fallback if we need something faster to demo.

Day 1 runbook highlights (attached: runbook-v1.md):
- Redwood: provision the PrivateLink service behind an NLB in our dedicated account, publish service DNS, and create an acceptance test harness. (Owner: Karthik)
- NetBridge: create interface endpoints in the NetBridge VPC and provide ENI quotas for test traffic. (Owner: NetBridge networkops)
- Security: enable mTLS on the control-plane endpoint and exchange certs via our security contact channel. (Owners: security teams)
- Throughput test: schedule a test window to validate sustained 2 Gbps for 15 minutes. If failure, fall back to an NLB+VPN tunnel for the batch window. (Owners: joint)
- Cost review: we'll produce a 12-month estimate including PrivateLink per-GB costs and expected egress; Sergio will own the commercial note for procurement.

Open items:
- NetBridge to confirm ENI quotas and any Service Quotas that would block interface endpoints.
- Procurement confirmation on accepting endpoint billing model.
- Provide us with the specific subnets they'd prefer for endpoint ENIs (we will avoid reserved ranges).

I've uploaded the runbook and a short proposal to a shared drive (link above). If no objections, we'll schedule the first integration run for next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook-v1.md (deployment checklist), connectivity-matrix.csv (updated)
